## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by strong evidence

Your sister's belief is correct and backed by high-quality scientific evidence — this is one of the better-studied claims about medical cannabis.

**Key evidence:**

1. **Pivotal RCT (Devinsky et al., NEJM 2017):** In a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 120 children/young adults with Dravet syndrome and drug-resistant seizures were randomized to add-on CBD (up to 20 mg/kg/day) or placebo. Convulsive seizure frequency dropped 39% with CBD vs. 13% with placebo — a statistically significant difference (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618).

2. **Confirmatory trials:** A second randomized trial testing different CBD doses (10 vs. 20 mg/kg/day) against placebo, published in *JAMA Neurology*, also found significant reductions in convulsive seizures with CBD (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458). A pooled analysis of two GWPCARE trials further confirmed the benefit (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/epi.17036).

3. **Systematic review/meta-analysis:** A 2020 meta-analysis in *CNS Drugs* synthesizing all available RCTs confirmed CBD's efficacy as adjunctive treatment for Dravet syndrome, alongside an acceptable (though not trivial) safety profile (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40263-020-00708-6).

4. **Regulatory recognition:** Based on this evidence, the FDA approved a pharmaceutical-grade CBD oral solution (Epidiolex) specifically for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome (and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome), marking the first cannabis-derived drug approval in the US.

**Important caveats:** This applies to a purified, pharmaceutical-grade CBD product (Epidiolex) at controlled doses — not over-the-counter CBD products, which vary widely in purity and dosing. Side effects (drowsiness, decreased appetite, diarrhea, liver enzyme elevations) are common, and CBD is used *as an add-on* to existing anti-seizure medications, not as a standalone cure. Seizure reduction, while significant, is partial — most patients still have seizures.
